title: Designing view transitions
description: Learn how to use view transitions to communicate meaning during navigation, loading, and content changes in a Next.js app.
nav_title: View transitions
---

In web apps, route changes replace the entire page at once. One set of elements disappears, another appears, with no visual connection between them. A user selects a photo thumbnail to view it in detail on another page. They are the same image, but nothing on screen communicates that.

Apps that need these transitions typically rely on complex animation libraries that manage mount/unmount lifecycles, track element positions across routes, and coordinate timing manually, to animate how elements enter, exit, and move between states.

React's `<ViewTransition>` component integrates with the browser's [View Transitions API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/View_Transition_API) to handle this declaratively. You name the elements that should persist, and the browser animates between their old and new positions.

part.text:
Build succeeded. Summary of changes:

**Files changed:**
- `app/ProductGrid.tsx` — wrapped each thumbnail in `<ViewTransition name="product-image-{slug}" share="morph" default="none">` and tagged every `<Link>` with `transitionTypes={['nav-forward']}`.
- `app/page.tsx` — wrapped the page in a directional `<ViewTransition>` keyed by `nav-forward`/`nav-back`, and wrapped the Suspense fallback with `exit="slide-down"` and the content with `enter="slide-up"`.
- `app/product/[slug]/page.tsx` — same directional wrapper, matching `name="product-image-{slug}"` on the hero for the morph, `transitionTypes={['nav-back']}` on the back link, and slide-up/slide-down on the detail Suspense.
- `app/globals.css` — added `::view-transition-*` rules for `.morph`, `.slide-up`/`.slide-down`, `.nav-forward`/`.nav-back`, plus `pointer-events: none` on the overlay and a `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` block that zeroes all animation durations/delays.
- `app/react-canary.d.ts` — `import type {} from 'react/canary'` so the `ViewTransition` type augmentation is loaded.

**Patterns applied** (from the Next.js view-transitions guide):
- Shared element: same `name` on grid thumb + detail hero with `share="morph"`, mid-flight blur keyframe.
- Suspense reveal: skeleton exit `slide-down` (fast) → content enter `slide-up` (delayed fade, longer slide).
- Directional slides: `transitionTypes` on `<Link>`, page-level `ViewTransition` mapping each type to an enter/exit class.
- Reduced motion: `animation-duration: 0s` on every `::view-transition-*` pseudo under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.
